classification: D. INDIVIDUAL SUSTAINABILITY NOT RELIABLY IDENTIFIABLE - DISTRIBUTIONAL UNCERTAINTY IS NEXT
basis: Frozen 2014-2020 evidence supports a high-end nonlinear source-magnitude relationship in Y3 absolute future points, with p90 the most stable tested slope-change coordinate but material boundary uncertainty remains.
Continuous D1H90 improves Y3 CRPS with uncertainty support but fails the preregistered p90+ bias-reduction gate and therefore does not earn authority.
No additional eligible ex-ante feature family passes the preregistered chronological identifiability gate.
Locked 2021-2022 replicates the high-magnitude Y3 retention gap and does not rescue either failed candidate.

Empirical exceptional-regime outcomes retain both productive-survivor and collapse/downside mass, so unresolved individual outcomes should remain in Forecast uncertainty/distribution shape rather than be forced into a higher mean.
